title: First single-target damage spell execution
objective: Prove that a presentation-independent enemy single-target damage skill can spend MP and mutate the same encounter-local target HP state already used by normal attacks.
hypothesis: Extending CombatantState with encounter-local MP and executing one explicitly supported SkillDefinition effect through CombatRuntimeRegistry will preserve the existing combat slice while establishing the first real spell mechanics path.
claim_boundary: This experiment does not map real GDB SkillInfo, does not implement original PAL3 magic formulas, does not create a Unity casting input/event seam, does not render VFX, and does not prove Unity compilation/runtime gameplay.

attempts.description: Add MP to encounter state; support DamageMagic + EnemyPartySingle + exactly one negative Absolute HP effect; reject unsupported mechanics before mutation.
attempts.expected_tests: existing 30 tests plus new single-target spell tests

reusable_lessons: Optional maxMp on CombatantState preserves all existing 3-argument construction sites while adding encounter-local MP.
Validate unsupported skill mechanics before spending MP or applying HP mutation; failed feature expansion must be transaction-like.
Skill casts can mutate the exact same CombatRuntimeRegistry state as normal attacks; no second shadow battle-state model is needed.

The source audit's NotSupportedException/throw marker counts increase when we add deliberate guardrails. Future workers must not interpret raw marker growth as implementation regression without file-level semantics.
Experiment logs should record an empty failures array when an attempt succeeds first try; never invent failure history.
next_recommended_experiment: Step 3: map real GDB SkillInfo into SkillDefinition without adding presentation assumptions, while preserving unsupported-field evidence explicitly.
